# Runtime APIs and external commands

## Scope

Choose between a runtime or platform API and an external command for a required capability. Own the semantic-fit assessment, command-boundary costs, and justification for retaining that interface when code is introduced, reviewed, or migrated into a language runtime.

## When to update

Update when evidence changes the criteria for semantic fit, command-boundary cost, justified retention, or verification of the selected interface.

## Compare interfaces

Start from required inputs, outputs, failures, lifetime, and supported environments. Prefer a runtime API when it supplies the required semantics and removes an unnecessary command boundary. An external system can be reached through more than one interface; requiring that system does not itself require its CLI.

## Account for arguments

Constructed shell text adds parsing and quoting. Pass separate argument values without a shell where the interface permits it; the target utility still interprets its own grammar.
documents.proposed_addition: An array-shaped parameter does not itself establish separate-argument transport. If a launch interface joins elements into command-line text, preserve intended value boundaries under its documented contract. Source-language string delimiters are not proof of child receipt. Verify the actual child argument count and values through the application's launch path. Apply this reasoning to any supported runtime and platform.
